description: Single-variable and introductory multivariable calculus with differential equations, taught with R and MATLAB alongside the pen so that every technique is also computed and plotted. Taught to the depth of a full first-year calculus sequence.
outcomes: Compute limits and derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions and apply them to rates, optimisation and curve sketching.
Evaluate definite and indefinite integrals by substitution, parts, partial fractions and trigonometric methods, and apply them to area, volume and average value.
Approximate integrals numerically with the trapezoidal and Simpson rules and bound the error.
Differentiate functions of several variables, find gradients, and locate and classify extrema.
Set up and evaluate double and triple integrals for areas, volumes and masses.
Solve first-order differential equations analytically and numerically and model growth, decay and cooling.

units.title: Functions, limits and continuity
topics: Review of functions, graphs, polynomials, rational, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Limits: intuition, one-sided limits, limit laws, squeeze theorem; limits at infinity
Continuity, types of discontinuity, intermediate value theorem
Plotting functions and estimating limits in R and MATLAB

units.title: Differential calculus
topics: Derivative as a limit, as slope and as rate of change; differentiability
Rules: power, product, quotient, chain; implicit and logarithmic differentiation
Derivatives of trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Applications: related rates, linear approximation, l'Hopital's rule
Mean value theorem; increasing and decreasing functions; concavity and curve sketching
Optimisation: maximising profit for a market stall, minimising material for a tank
Newton's method and symbolic differentiation in software

units.title: Integral calculus
topics: Antiderivatives and the indefinite integral; Riemann sums and the definite integral
Fundamental theorem of calculus
Substitution, integration by parts, trigonometric integrals and substitutions
Partial fractions and integration of rational functions
Improper integrals
Applications: area between curves, volumes of revolution, arc length, average value, work

units.title: Approximate integration
topics: Midpoint, trapezoidal and Simpson's rules
Error bounds and choosing the number of subintervals
Implementing the rules in R and MATLAB and comparing with built-in integrators
Taylor and Maclaurin series; using series to approximate integrals

units.title: Partial differentiation
topics: Functions of two and three variables; level curves and surfaces
Partial derivatives, higher-order partials, Clairaut's theorem
Tangent planes, differentials and the chain rule for several variables
Gradient and directional derivatives
Local extrema, second-derivative test, Lagrange multipliers

units.title: Multiple integrals and volumes
topics: Double integrals over rectangles and general regions; changing the order of integration
Double integrals in polar coordinates
Triple integrals; cylindrical and spherical coordinates
Applications: volume, mass, centre of mass, surface area

units.title: First-order differential equations
topics: Modelling with differential equations; direction fields
Separable and linear first-order equations; integrating factors; exact equations
Applications: population growth and logistic models, radioactive decay, Newton's law of cooling, mixing problems, RC circuits
Euler's method and Runge-Kutta in R and MATLAB; comparing numeric and exact solutions
A glimpse of second-order equations and oscillation

schedule.title: Functions and limits
schedule.exercise: Sketch six assorted functions (polynomial, rational, trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic) by hand with intercepts and asymptotes, then evaluate three limits using limit laws and one with the squeeze theorem.

tasks.title: Plot f(x) = x^3 - 4x and its shifted and stretched versions together, and read off the zeros and turning points from the graph
Plot a rational function with a removable discontinuity and a vertical asymptote and estimate both one-sided limits at each point from a table of values
Verify the squeeze theorem numerically for x^2 sin(1/x) near 0 by plotting the bounding functions and tabulating values at ever smaller x

schedule.title: Continuity and numerical limits
schedule.exercise: Classify the discontinuities of three given piecewise functions as removable, jump or infinite, and use the intermediate value theorem to show that x^3 + x - 1 has a root in (0, 1).

tasks.title: Plot a piecewise function with one jump and one removable break, and label each discontinuity type directly on the graph
Write an R or Python script that tabulates sin(x)/x for x approaching 0 from both sides and stops when successive values agree to six decimals
Implement bisection using the intermediate value theorem to locate a root of x^3 + x - 1 to within 1e-8 and count the iterations needed

schedule.title: Derivatives and differentiation rules
schedule.exercise: Differentiate ten functions using product, quotient and chain rules, including one implicit and one logarithmic differentiation, and check two of them with the limit definition.

tasks.title: Draw secant lines of f(x) = x^2 at x = 1 with shrinking h and watch the slope approach the tangent slope of 2
Differentiate five composite functions symbolically and plot each function with its derivative to confirm the zeros of the derivative match the turning points
Use implicit differentiation to find the tangent slope to x^2 + xy + y^2 = 7 at (1, 2) and confirm it by plotting the curve and the tangent line

schedule.title: Applications of derivatives
schedule.exercise: Solve a related-rates problem about a ladder leaning on a wall, then sketch a cubic curve fully using first and second derivative tests and state its intervals of increase and concavity.

tasks.title: Plot f(x) = x^3 - 3x and its derivative, and mark the increasing and decreasing intervals and the local maximum and minimum
Evaluate three indeterminate limits with l'Hopital's rule and confirm each numerically by tabulating the function near the limit point
Do a full curve sketch of x^4 - 4x^3 plotting f, f' and f'' together and identify extrema and inflection points from the sign changes

schedule.title: Optimisation and Newton's method
schedule.exercise: Model profit for a market stall selling bags of garri when price affects demand, and find the price maximising profit; then explain when Newton's method fails.

tasks.title: Find the dimensions of a rectangle of perimeter 40 m with the largest area by plotting area against width and checking with the derivative
Implement Newton's method for the root of cos(x) - x and print the error at each iteration to show quadratic convergence
Minimise the material for a closed cylindrical water tank of fixed 1000 litre volume, and confirm the optimum radius and height symbolically and by plot

schedule.title: Integrals and the fundamental theorem
schedule.exercise: Compute a Riemann sum with n = 4 and n = 8 for x^2 on [0, 2], then evaluate the exact integral with the fundamental theorem and compare the three values.

tasks.title: Draw left, right and midpoint Riemann sums for x^2 on [0, 2] with n = 4 and tabulate each approximation against the exact area
Evaluate five definite integrals with the fundamental theorem and verify each by plotting the integrand and the accumulated area function
Show numerically that the derivative of the accumulation function F(x) = integral of sin(t^2) from 0 to x equals sin(x^2) at 10 sample points

schedule.title: Techniques of integration
schedule.exercise: Integrate eight functions requiring substitution, integration by parts, trigonometric substitution or partial fractions, naming the technique chosen and the reason for each.

tasks.title: Integrate x*e^(x^2) by substitution and check the result by differentiating the antiderivative in the symbolic tool
Integrate x^2 ln x and e^x sin x by parts, and verify each antiderivative symbolically and by comparing definite values numerically
Decompose (3x + 5)/((x - 1)(x^2 + 4)) into partial fractions, integrate each part, and check the sum against the symbolic result

schedule.title: Improper integrals and applications
schedule.exercise: Decide convergence of three improper integrals by hand, then set up integrals for the area between two curves and the volume of a bowl formed by revolution.

tasks.title: Compute the area between y = x and y = x^2 on [0, 1] by integration and shade the region on a plot to confirm the bounds
Evaluate the integral of 1/x^p from 1 to infinity for p = 0.5, 1, 2 using truncated limits and tabulate which converge
Find the volume of the solid formed by revolving y = sqrt(x) about the x-axis on [0, 4] by discs and by shells, and compare the results

schedule.title: Numerical integration and series
schedule.exercise: Apply the trapezoidal and Simpson's rules with n = 4 to the integral of e^(-x^2) on [0, 1], compute the error bounds, and decide the n needed for error below 1e-6.

tasks.title: Code the trapezoidal rule and apply it to the integral of x^2 on [0, 3] with n = 6 and n = 12 to see the error shrink
Implement midpoint, trapezoidal and Simpson's rules, then compare their errors against the built-in integrator for n = 4, 8, 16, 32 on e^(-x^2)
Approximate the integral of sin(x)/x on [0, 1] using a Maclaurin series, find how many terms give error under 1e-8, and compare with Simpson's rule

schedule.title: Partial differentiation
schedule.exercise: For f(x, y) = x^2 + xy + y^2 - 6x, find the gradient, the critical points and classify them with the second-derivative test, then use Lagrange multipliers for the same f on x + y = 4.

tasks.title: Plot level curves of f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2 and x*y, and describe the surface shape each family of contours suggests
Compute the gradient of f(x, y) = x^2 y + sin(y) at (1, 0), plot it over the contour map, and find the directional derivative towards (1, 1)
Find and classify all critical points of x^3 - 3xy + y^3 using the Hessian, and verify the saddle and the minimum on a contour plot

schedule.title: Multiple integrals
schedule.exercise: Set up and evaluate a double integral over a triangular region in both orders of integration, then convert one integral over a disc to polar coordinates and evaluate it.

tasks.title: Evaluate the double integral of x*y over the rectangle [0, 2] x [0, 3] by iterated integration and check the result symbolically
Convert the integral of exp(-(x^2 + y^2)) over the unit disc to polar form, evaluate it exactly, and confirm with a numerical double integral
Compute the volume and centre of mass of a cone of uniform density using cylindrical coordinates and verify it with a Monte Carlo estimate of 100000 points

schedule.title: First-order differential equations
schedule.exercise: Model a cup of tea cooling in a Kumasi room with Newton's law, solve it by separation of variables, and use the solution to find when the tea reaches 50 degrees Celsius.

tasks.title: Plot the direction field of dy/dx = x - y and sketch the solution curves passing through (0, 1) and (0, -1)
Solve a linear equation y' + 2y = e^(-x) with an integrating factor and plot the solution family for three initial values
Fit the logistic model to a given Ghana population series, solve it exactly, and compare the predicted growth with the data on one plot

schedule.title: Numerical solution of ODEs and oscillation
schedule.exercise: Solve y' = y - x^2 + 1 with y(0) = 0.5 using Euler steps of 0.5 by hand, compare with the exact solution, and explain why a smaller step helps.

tasks.title: Code Euler's method for y' = -2y with y(0) = 1 on [0, 2] with step 0.2 and tabulate the error against the exact solution
Implement Euler and fourth-order Runge-Kutta for y' = y - x^2 + 1, and plot error against step size on a log scale for both methods
Solve y'' + 4y = 0 as a first-order system with Runge-Kutta, plot position against velocity, and check that the energy stays near constant
